scout.purpose: Generics reuse algorithms and containers while preserving the specific type of data moving through them.
scout.realWorldUse: Collections, Flow, repositories, serializers, UI state, navigation results, and dependency containers rely heavily on generic APIs.
scout.outcome: Declare bounded type parameters and reason about invariance, producers, consumers, and projections without unsafe casts.

blocks.text: A type parameter stands for a type chosen at each use site. Box<T> can hold an Expense or a String while keeping those uses distinct. Generic functions express relationships between input and output types that Any would erase. Constraints such as T : Comparable<T> restrict the accepted types to those providing required behaviour. Use a generic only when the implementation genuinely works across a family of types; a domain-specific function is clearer when rules depend on Expense semantics.

blocks.code:
data class Page<T>(
    val items: List<T>,
    val nextCursor: String?,
)

fun <T> Page<T>.isLast(): Boolean = nextCursor == null
blocks.caption: Page preserves its element type while reusable paging metadata and behaviour remain identical.

sections.title: Mutable generic types are invariant for safety

blocks.text: Even if CardExpense is a subtype of Expense, MutableList<CardExpense> is not a subtype of MutableList<Expense>. If it were, a function receiving the broader list could insert a CashExpense and corrupt the original collection. Read-only List is declared covariant because callers only receive elements. Variance describes how subtype relationships transfer through a generic type, not whether one value can be cast successfully in a particular test.

blocks.caption: Invariance prevents a broader writer from inserting the wrong subtype into a specialised mutable list.

blocks.title: Mutation changes variance
blocks.text: A type that both consumes and produces T is normally invariant because either direction alone would be unsafe.

sections.title: Use out for producers and in for consumers

blocks.text: A producer returns values of T but does not accept them, so it may declare out T. A consumer accepts T but does not return it, so it may declare in T. Remember “producer out, consumer in.” Declaration-site variance documents the whole type; use-site projections restrict one particular parameter. Star projections are useful when only non-type-specific operations are safe. Avoid adding variance until the API role is genuinely one-directional.

blocks.caption: The source only produces and the sink only consumes, allowing safe variance at each boundary.

blocks.text: Variance is an API promise checked across every member, so begin from how values cross the boundary rather than adding out or in until a compiler error disappears.

trap_check.mistake: Replacing a type parameter with Any and casting later.
trap_check.why: The compiler can no longer protect the relationship between inputs and outputs.
trap_check.fix: Express the relationship with a generic parameter and bounds.

trap_check.mistake: Marking T as out while accepting T in a public function.
trap_check.why: The consumer position contradicts the covariance promise.
trap_check.fix: Keep the type invariant or separate producer and consumer capabilities.

challenge_intro.task: Design generic Source and Sink APIs for importing expenses, with variance that allows specialised producers and broad consumers safely.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: No unchecked cast is required. Producer and consumer directions match their declarations. A specialised Expense source can copy into a sink that accepts Any.

recall.answer: It both accepts and returns elements, so broader substitution could corrupt its element type.

recall.prompt: What does a generic bound provide?
recall.answer: It restricts type arguments to values supporting required behaviour.

objectives: Preserve type relationships with generic classes and functions.
